one_line_description.value: Lark Open Platform provides server-side APIs that help developers access and modify data in the Lark system.
one_line_description.quote: Server-side APIs can help you access and modify data in the Lark system.

has_public_api.quote: Server-side APIs can help you access and modify data in the Lark system.

api_type.quote: Obtain the Contacts permission scope GET /open-apis/contact/v3/scopes

api_breadth.value: Broad multi-product REST API with read-write endpoints (Contacts users/groups, events, docs, messaging); e.g. create/update/delete users and user groups.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: Scopes are bound to API capabilities, data fields, and subscription events.

access_model.quote: Unlimited: Core features including Authentication and Authorization, Event Subscription, and Contacts are free to use, regardless of your Lark plan.

access_notes.value: Core auth, event subscription, and Contacts APIs are free regardless of Lark plan; Basic-tier usage is tallied and heavy users may need a higher-tier plan; Advanced APIs require a purchased quota package; sensitive scopes require app version submission and tenant administrator review; a test tenant/test app is available for development.
access_notes.quote: Manually approved scope: After requesting, you need to create an app version and submit it for review, and it will take effect only after the administrator reviews and approves it.

official_mcp_server.quote: lark-mcp is an MCP toolkit provided by the Lark Open Platform.

rate_limits.value: Tiered per API/app/tenant: levels 1-3 at 10/20/100 requests per minute; level 4 at 1000 requests/min and 50 requests/sec; custom bots 100/min and 5/sec; HTTP 429 with x-ogw-ratelimit-reset.
rate_limits.quote: The current API has a limit of 1000 times per minute and 50 times per second per application and tenant

webhooks.quote: Through event subscription, applications can respond to change events in Lark in a timely manner.

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: With the Test Companies functionality, the app created by the developer can be divided into official version and test version.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Event subscriptions are versioned v1.0 and v2.0, with v2.0 recommended; no general API deprecation/sunset policy appears in the provided sources.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: Open Platform provides two versions of events: v1.0 and v2.0. We recommend you to subscribe to the v2.0 events, as they offer more comprehensive and reasonable settings.

verdict_reason: Lark publishes a broad REST server API with documented access tokens, event subscriptions, and a large server API list. Core auth, event subscription, and Contacts APIs are free regardless of Lark plan, and a test tenant/test app supports development. Sensitive scopes require tenant-admin review and heavy or Advanced API usage requires paid plans or quota packages, but there is documented self-serve access rather than partner-only or sales-gated onboarding.
main_blocker: Sensitive scopes require tenant admin approval; paid quota for heavy API usage
open_questions: Official SDK languages could not be confirmed from the fetched SOURCES; a search snippet mentions Java/Golang/NodeJS SDKs but that page was not included in the evidence bundle.
The Lark-MCP FAQ lists 'Does Lark-MCP support remote SSE/Streamable HTTP endpoints?' but the provided text does not include an answer.
No general API deprecation/sunset policy was found in the provided sources; only event versioning (v1.0 vs v2.0) is documented in the evidence.
Community MCP servers were not verified; no GitHub or MCP registry results were supplied.
It is unclear whether a developer can create a free Lark tenant/app without any paid plan; the evidence only states core APIs are free regardless of plan and that a test tenant exists.
Rate-limit levels beyond the excerpts (level 5 and higher) are truncated in the provided source text.
App-name ambiguity was disambiguated using the input hint open.larksuite.com, which points to Lark/Larksuite rather than unrelated products named Lark.
